gemma-michael-jordan#eab539e7.summary: A loose cluster of "domain of activity" features: competition, skill, danger and injury, track-and-field athletes and volleyball history on one side, and academic research, scientific articles, markets and industries on the other, held together by generic "categories, activities, organizations" senses.

gemma-michael-jordan#43e43cf7.summary: Dominated by features for code snippets and programming keywords, reference codes, abbreviations and identifiers, with a secondary thread of scientific/technical jargon and legal language from court documents.

gemma-michael-jordan#16c0bd5c.summary: Almost every member is about sports as an organized competition: names of teams and players, league standings, injuries and statistics, with specific football and baseball features and one on sports leagues and championships.

gemma-michael-jordan#e7f75432.summary: Sports-semantics features centered on teams, athletic facilities and competitive physical activity, including an explicit basketball sub-cluster and one-off features for football, baseball and Formula 1 racing.

gemma-michael-jordan#b39f34b1.summary: Not a content group: these are document-mechanics detectors for the first word of a paragraph or title, sentences beginning with "It"/"In", the word "The", large runs of whitespace and left curly brackets, alongside code documentation, import statements and programming keywords.

gemma-michael-jordan#b477ece8.summary: A grab-bag of activity-domain features: athletics (competition, skill, injury, track-and-field athletes) mixed with academic and scientific research vocabulary, financial markets, nutrition and food deficiencies, and generic organization/category senses.

gemma-michael-jordan#1806ca8e.summary: A tightly basketball-focused group: basketball teams, terms and statistics, general sports-discussion words, and repeated features for sentences criticizing a basketball player's defensive abilities.

gemma-michael-jordan#5b2257c4.summary: Every member keys on playing rather than on sport specifically: gaming and gameplay vocabulary, and uses of the word "play"/"plays" alongside related words like "music" and "game".

gemma-michael-jordan#ab39644c.summary: Uniformly sports-semantics features spanning several disciplines: basketball and player contracts, soccer, football, plus teams, scoring, competition and statistics.

gemma-michael-jordan#b1433a7e.summary: Coherent around organized group activity: instances of group activities and challenges, team sports played in schools, and doing playful activities.

gemma-michael-jordan#e4f86894.summary: A small, uniform group covering sports and athletic activities generally, plus basketball-specific text about equipment and instruction.

gemma-michael-jordan#07348309.summary: Both members detect phrases indicating the role someone plays, especially in a movie, i.e. the theatrical rather than athletic sense of "plays".

gemma-small-big-fr#42c73a29.summary: A very large heterogeneous set with three recognizable threads: bulk scientific, medical and legal jargon plus code snippets at the embedding layers; French function-word features (the article "le", the preposition "de", the copula "est"/"to be"); and, in the deepest layers, French-language and code-switching detectors along with size and reversal words like "small", "inverse" and "vice versa".

gemma-small-big-fr#ff5b50e9.summary: The clearest thread is physical size: the word "small", dimensions, adjectives for small objects, and measurement/size nouns. Around it sit a large mass of scientific, medical and legal jargon and code features, plus quotation-mark and quoted-text detectors.

gemma-small-big-fr#44e9a0b1.summary: Unified by opposition and scale: features for "vice versa", "inverse", "reverse", things being contrary to something else, and change or reversal, paired with a small-to-big axis ("small", "Grand", "big", "too large", measurement adjectives). Background noise is the usual early-layer code and scientific jargon.

gemma-small-big-fr#94542751.summary: Three intertwined threads: heavy double- and single-quote detectors and quoted-string features, French grammar (the articles "le/la/les", French words, the verb "to be"), and size/quantity adjectives, all sitting on a bed of code and scientific-document jargon.

gemma-small-big-fr#441d36de.summary: Recurring copula features dominate — the French form of "to be", "est" as a suffix, the verb "to be" across languages and German "sein" — combined with a size thread ("small", "Grand", dimensions, size/quantity words) and the usual legal, technical and quoted-text background.

gemma-small-big-fr#5676029b.summary: French grammatical machinery is the backbone: "de", "le/la/les", French words and greetings, and the verb "to be". Layered on top are opposition features (the word "opposite", political opposition, negation and exceptions, reversed order) and a size/importance thread, plus lots of code and scientific jargon.

gemma-small-big-fr#3142bd92.summary: Mixed, but with three visible threads: mathematical and LaTeX notation plus code snippets, quotation-mark and quoted-title detectors, and a smallness thread ("small", "little" in the context of children) alongside French "de"/"le" and reversal features.

gemma-small-big-fr#d1352b94.summary: Largely quotation and citation machinery — text enclosed in quotation marks, quoted titles and names, references to academic publications, legal and journalistic writing — combined with French function words ("de", "le", "est") and a contrast/comparison thread.

gemma-small-big-fr#c3e67749.summary: The deep layers are strongly French: French words and language identification, French internet/computer chat, questions in French, and French opera, plus code-switching and non-English code. Earlier members contribute French articles and the copula, and scientific/technical terminology.

gemma-small-big-fr#a3fe2127.summary: French grammar features recur throughout — the preposition "de", the copula "est", French conversational text — mixed with a large amount of code, URL and scientific-document noise and, in the upper layers, quoted-speech, grammatical-discussion and academic-reference detectors.

gemma-small-big-fr#e9a6281f.summary: Heterogeneous but with recognizable threads: French articles and the copula ("le", "de", French text and "to be"), quotation-mark and emphasized-text detectors, and quantitative comparison features covering ratios, percentages, ranges, dimensions and size.

gemma-small-big-fr#182c5f50.summary: The consistent thread is scale and contrast: "grand", size/state/degree words, general importance or size, measurement adjectives, and explicit comparison-and-contrast phrases. Surrounding it are French "de"/"le" features, mathematical formulas, and multilingual code snippets.

gemma-small-big-fr#2cca55b1.summary: Opposition is the strongest thread — the word "other", political opposition and disagreement, "otherwise", contrast and comparison — alongside a size axis ("small", "grand", small quantities) and French conversational and multilingual features.

gemma-small-big-fr#e3786110.summary: Size adjectives recur at every depth: "small", "grand", "little" in the context of children, small quantities, general importance or size, and late-layer words describing intensity, size or level. Mixed in are French text and articles, debate/legal writing, and scientific document jargon.

gemma-small-big-fr#353656c0.summary: Language-identity features are prominent — German nouns and verbs, Danish text, French/Portuguese/Spanish pronouns and common words, verbs in non-English languages, translation definitions — together with a size thread ("grand", size adjectives, dimensions, small objects) and the usual scientific/technical jargon.

gemma-small-big-fr#0308e445.summary: The most semantically coherent of the large French groups: features for "otherwise", things being opposite or contrary, disagreement and contradiction, "vice versa"/"inverse"/"reverse", change or reversal, negativity and distance, and legal/military terms indicating opposition, over a background of code and scientific jargon.

gemma-small-big-fr#30fe4313.summary: Comparison is the recurring subject: "vs." comparisons, words used to compare one thing to another, versions and counterparts, conjunctions and quantifiers, and reversal words. These sit alongside "est"/"to be" copula features, French articles, quote detectors and code snippets.

gemma-small-big-fr#5fd501b1.summary: Built around French determiners and prepositions ("le/la/les", "de" and "de-" prefixes, French words) plus an opposition thread (the word "opposite", the word "other", political opposition and disagreement) and size adjectives, with scientific documents and math expressions as background.

gemma-small-big-fr#bd605f6a.summary: Mixes multilingual detectors — French, Danish, Portuguese and Croatian text, French/Scandinavian code, French political news — with comparison and opposition features ("vs.", the word "opposite", debate and disagreement) and a smallness/quantity thread, ending in French technical chat at the top layers.

gemma-small-big-fr#40172942.summary: French-language technical support output: Ubuntu and networking discussions, computer troubleshooting words, question-and-answer structure around "reponse", informal French chat, and code snippets, URLs and file paths.

gemma-small-big-fr#2ed676f0.summary: A shallow-layer detector cluster rather than a semantic one: many quotation-mark and quoted-string features, code snippets, programming terms and LaTeX/math symbols, legal and technical document vocabulary, proper nouns, and the French words "le" and "de".

gemma-small-big-fr#560ca0a9.summary: French-language output aimed at helping someone: conversational French chat and forum turns, Linux and Ubuntu usage instructions, networking and computer troubleshooting vocabulary, question/answer structure around "reponse", and accompanying code and URL snippets.
